newsitem.title: JAPAN: Ajinomoto says president to resign over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Ajinomoto says president to resign over scandal.

text.p: Ajinomoto Co Inc said on Friday that Shunsuke Inamori would step down as company president to take managerial responsibility for a scandal in which two company were officials were arrested and indicted on suspicion of making illegal payments to corporate racketeers.
Inamori will become the company's chairman, although he will have no voting rights on the board of directors regarding company business, Ajinomoto said in a news conference.
Managing director Kunio Egashira will replace Inamori as president, the company said.
The changes will be formally approved at a board meeting to be held at the end of June, the company said.

Ajinomoto, Japan's leading producer of seasonings and processed foods, said in March that two of its officials had been arrested on suspicion of paying several million yen in company funds to "sokaiya" racketeers in violation of Japan's commercial law. They were later indicted.
Ajinomoto conducted an in-house investigation after the scandal was revealed, but the company said on Friday that it had found no evidence that top officials were involved in any wrongdoing.
"No top officials were involved," managing director Egashira told the news conference.
Ajinomoto found, however, that checks and controls over the activities of its employees were insufficient, he said.
Entertainment expenses of one of the arrested officials totalled about one billion yen in the period from 1990 to 1996, Egashira said.
The company will soon set up an in-house committee to improve its management, Ajinomoto said.

Sokaiya, often linked to "yakuza" crime syndicates, typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices or to cause disturbances at shareholders' meetings, called "sokai" in Japanese.
